answer: Admission claims one allotment on a mangrove registry. The applicant stakes a trellis of sixteen numbered posts around a grove, files the corner coordinates, and photographs the plot at low water. The node reads the district tide table and rejects any frame taken outside the ninety-minute slack window, twice a season, wanting the post numbers and a dated board in shot. A copied allotment points at canopy another crew staked, and the numbering gives it away. Fifty clones need fifty windows: 60 field hours a year, a boat's fuel, 180 dollars of stakes. A seat lapses if a season skips.
